key_insight: MLP-mixer neural wave functions offer competitive quantum-state modeling, while a hierarchical mixer–transformer architecture outperforms other tested models on large quantum systems.
engineering_relevance: Lightweight information mixing offers a route to scalable classical simulation of quantum many-body systems while balancing correlation modeling and computational cost.
method: Use an MLP mixer as a wave function ansatz to mix information globally and locally.
Benchmark against RNNs and transformers with single-site and patched inputs.
Combine the mixer and transformer in a hierarchical architecture.
evidence_signal: Ground-state benchmarks on two-dimensional quantum many-body systems across phases and sizes assess representational accuracy and computational efficiency.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical speedups, error values, or resource requirements, limiting assessment of practical scaling gains.
paper_title: Scalable Neural Wave Functions via Information Mixing and Hierarchical Network Architectures
